rows.grounds: absolutive of niveśayati, to place or set down
absolutive of saṃsthāpayati, to establish or fix
compound kukkuṭa-āsana, cock seat or posture

items.question: What bodily configuration constitutes the cock-posture in this Kaula yoga instruction?
premises: The practitioner places something on the ground.
The practitioner establishes a fixed position.
The hair stands while assuming the posture.
items.inference: The cock-posture is performed with the body placed and established on the ground while the hair stands.
uncertainties: The exact referent of niveśya is not specified in this verse.
Whether romasthaḥ describes the practitioner or an accompanying sign is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Having placed on the ground and established the position, with hair standing, one assumes the cock-posture.
